package_info.why_malicious: This package version contains a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability (CVE-2017-8046) in the Spring Data REST and Spring Boot components. The flaw allows attackers to exploit unsafe data binding or deserialization in REST controllers, enabling arbitrary code execution on the server via crafted HTTP requests. This exposes affected systems to full remote compromise and makes the package version unsafe for any use.

execution_context.trigger: HTTP request to vulnerable REST endpoint at runtime
execution_context.file_location: org/springframework/data/rest/webmvc/RepositoryRestController.java (or related REST controller classes within the package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Defines a REST endpoint that processes incoming HTTP POST requests. The endpoint accepts user-supplied data in the request body and performs unsafe deserialization or data binding, allowing attackers to inject and execute arbitrary code on the server if malicious payloads are provided.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accepts and deserializes user-supplied input without proper validation or sanitization, exposing the application to remote code execution via crafted payloads. This is a well-known attack vector in Java applications, especially when using generic Object types for request bodies.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Standard REST endpoints should strictly validate and sanitize all user input, and never deserialize untrusted data into generic objects. They should not allow user input to influence code execution or system state beyond intended data processing.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate REST endpoints may deserialize user data into well-defined, type-safe objects with strict validation. However, they should never accept generic objects or perform deserialization without explicit type checks and input sanitization.
key_indicators: Use of @RequestBody with generic Object type
Lack of input validation or sanitization before deserialization
Deserialization or data binding of untrusted user input
Ability to trigger code execution via crafted HTTP POST requests

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP POST request with a malicious payload to the vulnerable REST endpoint.
attack_chain.leads_to: The vulnerable code deserializes the payload, allowing attacker-controlled code to be executed on the server.

attack_chain.action: Arbitrary code is executed with the permissions of the application process, potentially allowing the attacker to read, modify, or delete files, or execute further malicious actions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote control or executes malicious payloads on the server, potentially leading to full system compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected process execution or command invocation triggered by HTTP POST requests to REST endpoints
Deserialization of untrusted data in REST controllers, especially with generic Object types
Application log entries showing stack traces or errors related to deserialization or data binding
Unusual outbound network connections initiated immediately after REST endpoint access
file_indicators: Presence of vulnerable Spring Data REST or Spring Boot versions in dependency manifests (pom.xml, build.gradle)
References to org/springframework/data/rest/webmvc/RepositoryRestController or similar vulnerable classes
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP POST requests with suspicious or serialized payloads targeting REST endpoints
Outbound connections from application servers to external IPs or domains immediately following REST endpoint access
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs for deserialization or data binding errors, especially involving generic Object types. Use software composition analysis (SCA) tools to identify vulnerable versions of Spring Data REST and Spring Boot in dependency manifests. Inspect network traffic for suspicious inbound HTTP POST requests with serialized payloads and for unexpected outbound connections from application servers. Review code and configuration for use of @RequestBody with generic Object types in REST controllers.
